thread:
maria: heads up — we started getting multiple customer reports about generation latencies spiking around 09:03 UTC. p95 jumped from ~400ms to ~2.2s across several tenants. customers: tenant-42, tenant-98. sample request_id: r_8f6a3b2. logs show admission wait climbing and a lot of `admit_timeout` traces. can eng-oncall take a look? :rotating_light:

ops-bot: Alert: high_queueing_delay detected on inference-cluster-us-west
- metric: inference.request.p95 = 2.23s (5m)
- affected_pools: gen-dedicated-01, gen-dedicated-02
- active_admit_tokens: 82/120

lee: ack, I'm on it. Maria, can you paste a short repro or the customer API call? which model and route?

maria: payload we got from tenant-42 (trimmed):
```json
{
  "model": "redwood/gpt-helm-13b",
  "input": "<long chat history ~10k tokens>",
  "stream": false,
  "max_tokens": 1024
}
```
example curl we asked the customer to run (they did this against hosted):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-helm-13b","input":"test","max_tokens":512}' -o /dev/null -w '%{time_total}\n'
```
They reported typical time_total ~0.45s but now ~2.0-2.5s.

sam: looking at runtime metrics — we have a short burst of high-cost, long-context requests since 09:01 UTC. KV cache miss rate jumped ~4x, CPU saturation on gen-dedicated-02 nodes, and the admission controller has started queueing to enforce concurrency limits. stack excerpt:
```
worker_queue_len=128
admission.wait_ms_avg=450
admission.dropped=3
worker_active_concurrency=96/96
```
This matches the p95 regressions.

lee: thanks. Can we do a quick mitigation: 1) raise soft concurrency cap on gen-dedicated-02 from 96 -> 128; 2) enable fallback routing for non-SLA tenants to `redwood/compact-2b` where possible; 3) lower the admission controller target batch wait from 50ms -> 25ms to reduce queue accumulation. I'll take 1 & 3 if Sam approves.

sam: agree with mitigations. I'm going to roll a canary change to the admission controller config in the canary pool. Patch:
```yaml
admission:
  target_batch_ms: 25
  max_inflight_per_worker: 128
  preempt_long_queues: true
```
Applying to canary -> gen-dedicated-02-canary.

nora: I'll draft a short customer message template for tenants impacted. Suggested: "We're investigating increased generation latencies; short-term mitigation applied and you may see improved latency within minutes. We'll follow up with a root-cause update." Want me to send to tenant-42 and tenant-98 now?

maria: please send to tenant-42 now, tenant-98 after we confirm canary behavior. include the request_id r_8f6a3b2 and say we're tracking.

ops-bot: deploy-bot triggered: Created rollout job admission-config-canary-2120001111 -> gen-dedicated-02-canary

deploy-bot: rollout started (canary) — job id j-7321. logs streaming to /var/logs/rollouts/j-7321

sam: canary applied. early telemetry: admission.wait_ms dropped to 120ms in canary, worker_queue_len down ~60%. p95 in canary pool falling to ~600ms.

lee: good signal. I'll promote the config to the rest of gen-dedicated pool in 10 minutes if metrics hold. also enabling fallback routing in routing rules for non-SLA rate classes, patch queued.

maria: customers notified (tenant-42 updated). tenant reported latency back to ~700ms after the canary change.

nora: copied legal & account teams for tenant-98 (they're on contract), starting a scheduled update for them in 30m.

sam: after we stabilize I'll follow up with a deeper root cause: my current hypothesis is a recent shift in traffic composition: 1) more long-context / streaming-batch requests leading to KV cache churn, 2) reduced kernel-level batching efficiency for large seq lengths, which increases per-token compute and blocks worker concurrency. We'll collect webhook traces and kernel utilization.

lee: short-term action items:
- [sam] own canary -> prod rollout and perf dashboards (owners)
- [lee] monitor for 2h, rollback plan ready if p95 > 1.5s
- [maria] customer comms and collect any repro payloads
- [nora] coordinate account communications for enterprise tenants
- [ops-bot] keep alert on suppressed mode for 30m

maria: one more repro tip collected from tenant-98: they hit an automated retry loop when requests returned 429-like internal admission stalls. sequence: 1) client times out after 3s, 2) client retries, 3) retries add to the burst. recommend ops update SDK timeouts for long-context routes and expose a `retry_after` header when admission backpressure is active.

sam: good catch. I'll add a short-term header `X-Redwood-Retry-After` with seconds when admission queue depth > 80% in the next runtime patch. longer-term we'll add backpressure signals to SDKs.

lee: rolling to prod now. promoting config across gen-dedicated-01/02.

ops-bot: rollout j-7321 promoted to prod.

deploy-bot: rollout finished successfully.

sam: post-promotion telemetry: cluster-wide p95 dropped from 2.2s -> 680ms, p99 from 3.9s -> 1.6s. KV cache miss rate down ~30%.

maria: customer confirmations trickling in, tenant-42 marks as resolved.

nora: sending update to tenant-98 now, including: summary of mitigation, expected follow-up (root-cause + postmortem), and ETA for SDK/backpressure improvements.

lee: leaving monitoring on for 120 minutes. Sam — please own the postmortem and include: traffic composition change, kernel/batching impact, admission thresholds, and recommended longer-term mitigations (adaptive concurrency, better retry headers, SDK changes).

sam: will do. I'll start a draft and link to this thread + perf dashboards.

maria: thanks team — closing this thread once the postmortem link is up. cc @nora for customer comms. :white_check_mark:
